opening: Your Atmos stack, with choudoufu as the component command. This second act adds a subnet to network. Its id is known only after apply.

pull-request.prompt: Add a second subnet to network; put a worker in it.
pull-request.reply: Opened pull request {pull}. network adds subnet b and app adds a worker in it, and edge allows the range.

pull-request.status: The workflow runs atmos terraform plan on the estates component

planned.reply: One plan across 3 estates. Only one value is unknown: subnet b's id, which app's worker needs.

planned.prompt: Why is app's plan a guess?
planned.reply: app reads network with !terraform.output, which reads applied state. App's plan uses a default or a mock until network applies, or fails.

planned.prompt: What depends on the new subnet?
planned.reply: Two resources depend on it: app's worker and edge's allowlist.

approved.status: Recording your approval as a review on the pull request

merged.status: Merging; the workflow runs atmos terraform apply

tips: Ordered deployments apply parents first. The child's plan still can't see an id that doesn't exist yet.

applied.reply: Done. Subnet b was created and app's worker got its id in the same apply.
Never. choudoufu holds no lock to leave behind, so there is nothing to force-unlock. Each record is written only if it is unchanged since it was read: resource-level locking at the cloud level.
